The Ultimate Gaming experience for your company

Covid-19 changed the way teams in your company bond. Esports Business League is a team building charity esports event, where your company team can compete against teams from other companies. Participants in the Esports Business League so far include companies like VMware, DXC, SAP, Experian, TELUS, Modis, HP, Infragistics, Chaos Group and many more!

Esports Business League is a charity esports event, which provides working gamers with an arena for competition between individuals and teams from different companies. Each season of the league is 4-8 weeks in length. Matches take place on week days after working hours Monday-Thursday. The league culminates with finals where the teams and players who have accumulated the most points during the season meet. All league matches are being broadcasted live on our Twitch channels.
Groups of up to 8 teams competing in a round-robin format across 3-7 weeks. Matches on weekday evenings, capped off by a grand finals weekend. All matches are streamed live!
Groups of up to 8 players competing in a round-robin format across 3-7 weeks. Matches on weekday evenings, capped off by a grand finals weekend. All matches are streamed live!

All team members must be current employees of the registered company, with no active professional esports affiliation and no professional matches in the past 24 months. Standins must meet the same conditions.
StarCraft II competitors must be current employees of their registered company. Substitutes may be added post-registration under the same eligibility conditions.
300 BGN per Counter-Strike team · 60 BGN per StarCraft II player. Paid via bank transfer after form submission. Limited to 16 teams / 32 players.
All registration fees form the prize pool, which is fully donated to a charitable cause chosen by the winners at the end of each season.
BPro Gaming is the first professional esports club in Bulgaria. During the past 4 years BPro has developed a number of professional players, team and infrastructure.

BSL a one of a kind StarCraft II league in Bulgaria and are contributing to the deveopment of Bulgarian talent in this esport! All StarCraft 2 games in the Esports Business League will be casted by the them!

The winning team/player will appropriate 75% of the prize pool towards their choice of a charitable cause.
The runner-up will appropriate 25% of the prize pool towards their choice of a charitable cause.

Season 2 concluded on November 8th with grand finals in both StarCraft II and Counter-Strike. SuGaRBuNNy [Nuvei] claimed the SC2 title after a nail-biting BO5, while Plan-B [Modis] swept both maps to take the CS:GO crown.

Season 1 ended on April 12 with grand finals in both StarCraft II and Counter-Strike. SuGaRBuNNy [C3I] won a competitive BO5 to claim the SC2 title, while Bpro Veterans triumphed in a 3-map thriller over DXC.

Esports Business League is organized by Bellum Gens — an organization focused on the development and popularization of esports in Bulgaria and on the Balkans. We want to make esports a recognizable topic for the business community and help all esports projects in the region grow.

Teams from the Counter-Strike league will be separated into groups of 4-8 teams.
Each team plays 1-2 matches a week against other teams from the same group. At the end of the group stage, the best teams of each group go to the finals.
Players from the StarCraft II league will be separated into groups of 4-8 players.
Each player plays 1-2 matches a week against other players from the same group. At the end of the group stage, the best players of each group go to the finals.

Group stage matches are being played weekly Monday-Thursday. All matches are played sequentially in the evening, after working hours, starting from 7:30pm EET. Each match except the first one starts 15 minutes after the previous match has finished. Weekly schedule for the entire group stage would be available prior to the league start date. The schedule is subject to change, if and only if a participant has managed to reach an agreement with all other affected participants by the change.

Weekly matches are in best-of-one (BO1) or best-of-three (BO3) format with map veto on the current active duty maps at the start of the league. The map veto takes place 10-15 minutes prior to the match and is performed by the team captains and an admin. Which side teams start on is decided either by the team not picking the map, or with a knife round, the winner of which picks the side. Each map is played until one of the teams wins 16 rounds and teams are switching sides after 15 rounds have been played. If there's no winner after 30 rounds - score is 15-15 - then the match goes into overtime. Each overtime is 6 rounds in length and each team starts on the side the team has been before the start of the overtime. Teams are switching sides in overtime after 3 rounds have been played. If an overtime reaches a score of 3-3, then a new overtime is played. Each player starts an overtime with maximum cash - $16000 - so each round of the overtime is a guaranteed gun round.

Weekly matches are in best-of-three (BO3) format with map veto with 2 bans and 2 picks from the maps in the current ladder pool at the start of the league. The map veto takes place 10-15 minutes prior to the match, and is performed by the players, the match caster and an admin. Each map is played until one of the two players emerges victorious. The 3rd decider map is played only in the case of a 1-1 score.

Tournament participants are being separated into groups and the first opponents are being drawn. Each group has two brackets - winners and losers bracket. All participants start in the winners bracket and after a loss are being moved to the losers bracket. Participants are eliminated after they accumulate a loss in the losers bracket.

Each match in the group stage of the league gives the teams between 0 and 3 points. After all group stage matches have been played, the 2 teams with the most points from each group proceed to the finals. If two teams have equal points, then round difference is taken into account. In the case of equal points and round difference, the result of the direct duel between the two teams is taken into account.
3 points for a win in regulation
2 points for a win in overtime
1 point for a loss in overtime
0 points for a loss in regulation

Each match in the group stage of the league gives the participants between 0 and 3 points. After all group stage matches have been played, the 2 players with the most points from each group proceed to the finals. In the case of equal points, the result of the direct duel between the two participants is taken into account.

Usage of assistive software of any kind, which can be classified as a cheat, is strictly forbidden. Each match in the league would be streamed live and would be moderated by an admin. In the case of a suspicion of cheating, the case will be investigated by the admins and if the admins conclude that theres evidence beyond a reasonable doubt for cheating, then the player (StarCraft II), or team (Counter-Strike), which the player participates in would be disqualified!!! Esports Business League is an amateur event, where players need to show their own abilities, and not the abilities of a software which assists and alters their gameplay. Our goal is to provide the best experience for all participants!
